summary.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; spot trade prices ~5% above Q2 average entering Q3.
summary.overview: UltraTech reported a strong Q2 FY27 on volume growth of 13.8% and a 21% rise in net profit, despite fuel costs rising sharply on the West Asia conflict. Q2 average trade prices were flat to Q1 (down 1-1.5%), but prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in late September and kept rising in October, with management putting spot about 5% above the Q2 average. Fuel cost rose from INR 45 to INR 51.5 per bag, and management expects the cost pressure to largely persist through Q3-Q4 at roughly INR 2.2 per kcal. Capacity reached 204.7 Mt domestic after 4.6 Mt commissioning in September, and the Ultravolt wires and cables business launched on 3 September. Net debt rose to 1.26x net debt/EBITDA from 0.94x at March-end.

segments.name: Cement - North
segments.commentary: Volumes grew more than 20% YoY; utilisation upwards of 70%; new prices absorbed.

segments.name: Cement - South
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 15-20% YoY on about 50 Mt capacity; utilisation above 70%; capacities fully sold out; prices improving. A greenfield plant was commissioned this quarter.

segments.name: Cement - West
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 10%; utilisation close to 70%; Mumbai prices up 3-4% per bag in September.

segments.name: Cement - East
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 5%; utilisation about 60% due to heavy monsoon; prices fell in August and are now catching up since early October.

segments.name: Cement - Central
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 10%; utilisation about 60%; pricing described as muted.

segments.name: Ultravolt (wires and cables)
segments.commentary: Launched 3 September 2026; about 25-27 days of operation in Q2. INR 1,100 crore of INR 1,800 crore capex spent or committed; 80,000+ retail points and 1,500+ UBS channel partners signed up; management says it will not talk about revenue or margin yet and expects a meaningful quarter in April-June 2027. Expense attributable to the business is not material per management.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 capex guidance held at about INR 10,000 crore (plus or minus); fuller view promised after Q3 results.
Full benefit of recent price increases expected to reflect in Q3 earnings rather than immediately; management intends to sustain YoY higher EBITDA per ton over the next two quarters.
Pet coke and fuel cost: management sees the INR 2.2/kcal level persisting through Q3-Q4 if $180/t pet coke holds; marginal impact expected in Q4 from inventory pipeline.
Targets 240 Mt capacity as planned; next organic growth phase to be announced before FY27 end, with detailed plans to come.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1x by March 2027.
Business-as-usual delivery of INR 1,400/t EBITDA exit-March 2028 target; cost pressures expected to be covered by price increases.
Ultravolt maturity expected by FY28; Board has not sanctioned capex beyond INR 1,800 crore; target revenue reference of INR 10,000 crore now seen at INR 16,000-18,000 crore on copper prices.
Industry demand expected to grow close to 8% in H1 FY27 and to remain strong through March 2029.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 4.6 Mt in September 2026, including the 3.6 Mt greenfield at Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) and 1 Mt debottlenecking at three units; domestic capacity now 204.7 Mt.
On track for 240 Mt capacity as planned.
Added 116 MW renewable power and 10 MW waste heat recovery; 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use.
AFR systems commissioned at 2 plants; thermal substitution rate about 7.2%.

Ultravolt: INR 1,800 crore plan with about INR 1,100 crore spent or committed; balance expected over about two quarters; mother plant at Jhagadia, Gujarat; 78,000 tpa copper consumption capacity annualised.
demand_pricing: Q2 average trade prices flat vs Q1 (down about 1-1.5%) due to soft August; trade prices rose 7-10 per bag MoM in late September, and exit-September trade was at least about 3% above Q1 average.
Spot realisations in October about 5% above Q2 average, per management.
Trade ratio stable at 65-67% (65.7% in Q2 per management); premium cement 37% of sales; blended cement 67.3%.
Over 25% of trade sales come through the UBS network (about 6,500 stores, target 10,000 by FY28-29).
Industry demand close to 10% YoY in Q2; management says the Q1 industry rate was 6.5%.
Fuel costs: pet coke about $180/t; pet coke share cut to about 25% of mix; domestic coal supply constrained as Coal India prioritises power sector.
Public infrastructure awards picking up; central capex strong through July; road construction weak.

qa_highlights.question: Variable cost inflation in H2 at current spot levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify but noted inventory in the pipeline means Q3 impact is limited and marginal impact in Q4; expects not much additional inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Tamil Nadu levy of INR 160/t: accounted in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is already accounted for in Q2 with no reversal, and the company incurs no additional cost from the effective date.

qa_highlights.question: Capex guidance and H1 capex of INR 5,882 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held full-year capex at about INR 10,000 crore plus or minus, to be refined after Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise about 22% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore NCDs at 7.25% were raised and held for about two months; management said the borrowing was a good decision given current rates.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt increase in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex and dividend payment; net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March-end, with expected to fall below 1x by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is trade volume demand housing-led or industrial-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade ratio stable at 65-67%, indicating retail housing demand holds share; industrial volumes growing faster; industry sold 463 Mt in FY26 vs UltraTech 145 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: Ultravolt capacity and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 10,000 crore revenue target from early 2025 could reach INR 16,000-18,000 crore at current copper prices; no further capex beyond INR 1,800 crore sanctioned; production to double from current levels.

risks_watch: Fuel and energy costs: pet coke about $180/t, domestic coal constraint, and industrial diesel at record highs; West Asia conflict outcome uncertain.
Weak monsoon (fourth lowest since 2001) and drought pockets could soften rural demand.
Ultravolt ramp-up: stock-outs possible, unproven margins, and no revenue disclosure yet; separately reported from next quarter as a division of the standalone financials.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x; capex and dividend are funding needs.
Festive-season slowdown may delay full realisation of price increases until Q3 results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and volume momentum, with specific numbers for most questions, but evasive on Ultravolt margins and utilisation and on H2 cost inflation. Management repeatedly deflected to "give us some time" for the new business and declined to quantify cost trajectory beyond INR 2.2/kcal.
key_quotes: We are on track to reach 240 million tons of capacity as planned without any surprises.
Our growth of 13.8% this quarter is comfortably ahead, which means that our presence in the market is continuously increasing.
So now the prices are leading the way.
Cement is our core. We are growing very strongly in cement.

financial_highlights.change: Ahead of industry growth of close to 10%
Absolute fixed costs up 4% vs volume up 13.8%

adds.what: 3.6 Mt greenfield Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) commissioned Sept 2026, plus 1 Mt debottlenecking at three units; domestic capacity now 204.7 Mt
Ultravolt wires and cables plant, mother plant at Jhagadia Gujarat (78,000 tpa copper consumption capacity)
Target 240 Mt cement capacity as planned; next organic growth phase to be announced before FY27 end

growth.why: Brief reports 13.8% volume growth and 21% net profit growth in Q2 with spot prices about 5% above Q2 average and 204.7 Mt capacity after 4.6 Mt commissioning, but no explicit FY27 revenue growth guidance; the 240 Mt target lacks a dated timeline and FY27 capex is held at about INR 10,000 crore.
